verdict.reasoning: Patient reports, “over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath” while “sitting watching TV,” indicating acute onset over ~1 hour while sitting.
Patient states, “So I started with a cough yesterday” and when asked if she has brought anything up replies, “No, I haven't. No,” indicating a new non-productive cough since yesterday.
When asked, “have you noticed anything like this before?” the patient answers, “No,” indicating no prior episodes of shortness of breath.
Clinician asks, “And the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest?” and patient replies, “No,” indicating no chest pain associated with the shortness of breath.
When asked about deep breath, patient says, “I mean, yeah, my chest feels sore,” indicating chest discomfort on deep inspiration.

Clinician asks, “apart from the C section and the shortness of breath. Have you got any other medical problems I should know about?” and patient answers, “No,” indicating no other medical problems reported.
When asked about the baby: “Any coughs or colds with them?” patient replies, “No, no, he's fine,” indicating the baby is well without coughs or colds.
Patient reports, “I had a C section a few weeks ago,” and clarifies, “Yeah. Four weeks,” confirming cesarean section 4 weeks ago.

Patient says, “They gave me some codeine,” and, “Yeah, I've been taking that fairly regularly, but probably haven't taken it for a week,” indicating postoperative codeine use with last dose about a week ago.
Patient states, “I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though.” When asked what happens, she replies, “I don't know,” so the allergy is to ibuprofen with unclear reaction details.
Patient notes, “my mum's had clots in her legs before,” indicating maternal history of leg clots.

Transcript confirms baby is with her (“And are you with baby at the moment? ... Yes, I am.”) and that her partner is at work (“No, my partner's at work.”). It does not explicitly state that she lives with her baby; inferring living arrangement is additional information.
Patient self-counts pulse: clinician times and asks, “How many did you count?” Patient replies, “I counted 30.” The exact timeframe is not specified in the transcript, matching the statement.

Beyond the self-counted pulse, no other physical examination findings or formal vital signs (e.g., BP, RR, O2 sat, temperature) are documented in the transcript, so stating there are none documented is consistent.

Clinician notes heart “running slightly fast” after pulse count and says, “Given that you've had a C section and you're short of breath… it might be worth you going into the hospital… What I'm worried about… is… some people can suffer with clots… in your lungs,” indicating concern for pulmonary embolism due to acute SOB, tachycardia, and recent C-section.
The cough is described as starting yesterday and non-productive, and no specific cause is identified or discussed; thus, stating that the etiology is unclear is consistent with the transcript.
Patient had a C section 4 weeks ago and is still recovering (tender chest and C-section scar, codeine use), supporting that she is in postoperative status from cesarean section.

Clinician advises, “it might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further” and later explains concern about clots in the lungs and treatment, implying ED evaluation for possible pulmonary embolism.
Clinician states, “And if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them for the time being,” indicating plan to hold codeine.

Clinician offers ambulance vs self-transport: “I can call an ambulance or you can take yourself to the hospital with baby. Which one would you prefer?” Patient replies, “I'll go. I'll take myself,” confirming she will arrange her own transport with baby.

Clinician explains concern about clots (“some people can suffer with clots… in your lungs… needs to be checked out”), mentions treatment (“they can give you something to reduce the clot”), and reassures about process, which constitutes counseling regarding symptoms, risks, and management.
The transcript includes advice to go to hospital “fairly quickly” but does not document explicit instructions to monitor for worsening symptoms while en route; this specific directive is not stated.
